newsitem.title: USA: US may take action on Japan insurance - Barshefsky.
newsitem.headline: US may take action on Japan insurance - Barshefsky.

text.p: Acting U.S. Trade Representative Charlene Barshefsky said Thursday the United States would "respond appropriately" if Japan took action that would violate a 1994 trade agreement on insurance.
Barshefsky told a USTR advisory committee that any negotiated settlement would have to be "fully consistent" with the commitments made in the 1994 agreement.
The United States and Japan have been trying for a year to resolve a dispute over the 1994 agreement on deregulation of Japan's insurance market and more talks are scheduled for next week.

The dispute centers on deregulation of Japan's insurance market and a proposal by the Ministry of Finance to deregulate the small specialty insurance sector, in which foreign companies enjoy a large share, before deregulating the huge primary life and casualty markets.

"Should MOF take action which in our view contravenes commitments under the insurance agreement we will respond appropriately," Barshefsky said. She did not say what actions the United States would take.
